_comment: DECLARED STATE of the Cloudflare estate. Written 2026-08-20 after an R2 lifecycle
misconfiguration billed $9.00/month for four days before anyone looked.
This file is the answer to 'what is supposed to be deployed'. ops\audit-cloudflare-estate.ps1
reads it and compares against live. Nothing else in this repo referenced these buckets, this
database, or these workers at all before today - they were created 2026-08-09/10 by the deleted
V3 platform estate and have been changing costs silently ever since.
READ docs\RUNTIME-MAP.md BEFORE DELETING ANYTHING HERE. It says the tc-grocery-v3 worker is
'no longer in any serving path'. That is WRONG and measured wrong on 2026-08-20: tc-grocery-v3
took 480 requests in five days, more than smp-feed, and all 542 live recipe cards hydrate their
prices from a route it serves. The V3 code was deleted from the repo; the V3 runtime was not.

infrequentAccessWhy: R2 operations are billed per WHOLE MILLION and are not prorated, and the Infrequent Access
class has no free tier. One single lifecycle transition anywhere in the account therefore buys
a full $9.00 Class A block. On 2026-08-19, 499 transitions cost $9.00 - a rate of $0.018 per
The saving it buys is $0.005/GB-month. At the estate's ~42GB that is about $0.06 a month, and
moving out of Standard also forfeits the 10GB Standard free tier. Break-even is roughly 1.8 TB.
Do not add a storageClassTransition to any bucket below unless IA holds more than 1.8 TB.
Partial cleanup is worthless: it is one $9.00 block per cycle regardless of volume, so leaving
even ONE IA transition anywhere in the account costs the full $9.00.

rules.id: Bound encrypted capture journal recovery points

retentionGap: release-nodes/schema=1/, observations/schema=1/ and release-manifests/schema=1/ have NO expiry
and grow forever. 60,034 objects / 4.2GB on 2026-08-20, currently creeping ~5 objects/day.
Three rules that used to cover these prefixes did nothing but move them to Infrequent Access -
no delete transition at all - so they were removed outright on 2026-08-20 rather than stripped
(the API rejects a rule with no transition left). Removing them changed no data and no retention,
because they never deleted anything. Deciding an actual TTL here is still an open question.

rules.id: Archive weekly D1 exports then expire
Archive independent backup replica then expire

observed: 4.03GB on 2026-08-20 and FALLING ~0.075GB/day since the 2026-08-15 peak of 4.38GB.
Storage is the binding D1 constraint, not rows: 81% of the 5GB included, overage $0.75/GB-month.
The 2026-08-12..14 backfill took it 0.88GB -> 4.36GB in two days. A second backfill of that size
would cross 5GB. Rows written run ~257k/day steady (~8M/month of 50M included) but that same
backfill wrote 14M rows in ONE day, so four such days would also cross the row allowance
at $1.00/million. Rows read (~8.5M/day of 25B) are not a constraint and never have been.

tc-grocery-v3.status: LIVE - busiest worker on the account despite RUNTIME-MAP.md calling it dead
